# L&D Energy — EPC Certificates London

## What we do
L&D Energy is the EPC trading division of Luminous & Deliver Ltd. We are an Elmhurst-accredited Domestic Energy Assessor (DEA) providing official Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs) and professional floor plans for residential properties across all 32 London boroughs plus the City of London.

## Key facts
- Accreditation: Elmhurst Energy (UK's largest DEA accreditation scheme)
- Coverage: All London boroughs — from Stratford (our base) to Hillingdon, Enfield, and Croydon
- Base location: Stratford, East London, E15
- Contact: 07492 575 396 | contact@luminousanddeliver.co.uk
- Hours: Monday–Sunday, 8am–8pm

## Services and pricing
All figures are guide estimates and act as starting prices. The final cost depends on the property's floor area (m²), any extensions or loft conversions, layout, and condition. There is no charge for travel or mileage; properties more than about 45 minutes away add a little for the extra time, not the distance.

Estate and letting agents: we act as an EPC and floor plan supplier for London agencies, with volume rates, fast turnaround on new instructions, and certificates delivered direct to branch. We are currently taking on new agency clients. Details: https://epc.luminousanddeliver.co.uk/estate-agents

## EPC delivery
- Standard: within 72 hours of the assessment
- Express (next-day): within 24 hours of the assessment
- Certificate emailed as PDF and lodged on the UK Government EPC Register

## What is an EPC?
An Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) rates a property's energy efficiency on a scale from A (most efficient) to G (least efficient). It is a legal requirement in England and Wales when selling or renting a property. EPCs are valid for 10 years.

## Legal requirement
An EPC is required by law:
- When letting a residential property (minimum rating: E)
- When selling a residential property
- For newly built homes
- Landlords must have a minimum EPC rating of E (band E) under the Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES). Proposed future legislation may raise this to C by 2028.
